targets.title: Top-Down Modulation of Motor Priming by Belief About Animacy
targets.evidence_quote: One of the most prominent studies supporting such an influence is the study by Liepelt & Brass (2010), who found that automatic imitation was stronger when participants believed an ambiguous, gloved hand to be human, as opposed to wooden. In this registered report, we provide a high-powered replication of this study (N = 199).
targets.outcome_quote: In contrast to Liepelt & Brass (2010), we did not find an effect of animacy beliefs on automatic imitation.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The central animacy-belief effect was not replicated; exploratory exclusion results do not replace the central verdict.
